references.text: Moses had previously been commanded to stretch out his hand over the sea, which he now carries out in verse 21.
Describes the result of the parting of the waters, where the Israelites walked on dry ground through the sea.
Moses' song of praise describes how God's spirit (wind) gathered the waters and let them stand as a wall.
The psalmist reminds us how God turned the sea into dry land.
Refers to God's power over the sea, which parted it with His strength.
Retells how God split the sea and let the Israelites walk through it.
Describes how God threatened the Red Sea so that it became dry, and led the people through the depths.
Poetic description of the sea fleeing when Israel left Egypt.
Praises God who parted the Red Sea in two and led Israel through it.
Isaiah reminds us of the Lord's arm which dried up the sea and made the depths of the sea a road.
Refers to God who led Moses by His right hand and split the water before them.
Nehemiah retells how God split the sea before the Israelites so that they walked on dry ground.
Joshua compares the crossing of the Jordan with the crossing of the Red Sea.
The book of Hebrews mentions that the Israelites in faith went through the Red Sea as if it were dry land.
Paul refers to the fathers who passed through the sea and were baptized into Moses in the cloud and in the sea.
Describes the immediate conclusion of the parting of the sea, where God's salvation is completed by turning the water back against the enemy.
Illustrates how God uses the same natural forces (the east wind) both as judgment upon Egypt and as an instrument for deliverance.
